sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: residents versus visitors, renewal channels, point thresholds and restricted licenses
Confusable pairs among residency rules, renewal channels, point thresholds and the licenses available during a suspension, followed by continuation facts; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec02-R01 | anchor: A01
The first skills retest wait is counted in business days, while the second and later waits are counted in calendar days. [A01]
Why it matters: group skills retest; confusable business versus calendar days.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-R02 | anchor: A01
A person moving to SC permanently must switch to an SC license within 45 days, while a temporary resident such as a student may keep driving on a valid out-of-state license. [A01]
Why it matters: group residency; confusable permanent versus temporary move.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-R03 | anchor: A01
Active-duty military members and US Government employees are the two groups excused from the 45-day deadline for new permanent residents. [A01]
Why it matters: group residency; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-R04 | anchor: A02
A visitor who lives permanently in another state, for example New York, can drive in SC on that state's valid license. [A02]
Why it matters: group residency; confusable visitor versus new resident.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R05 | anchor: A02
An International Driving Permit is used together with a valid foreign license so that officers can read it, and it does not count as a license by itself. [A02]
Why it matters: group international; confusable permit as translation versus license.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R06 | anchor: A03
The vision certificate is accepted when dated within 36 months, while a military Leave and Earning Statement must be dated within 31 days of the transaction. [A03]
Why it matters: group renewal; confusable thirty-six months versus thirty-one days.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R07 | anchor: A03
Active-duty personnel renewing by mail or online send copies of the Leave and Earning Statement and the non-expired military ID by mail or email. [A03]
Why it matters: group renewal; difficulty high.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R08 | anchor: A04
Online renewal is closed to anyone with more than five points on the record in the last two years, even if every other condition is met. [A04]
Why it matters: group renewal; confusable renewal point limit versus suspension thresholds.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-R09 | anchor: A04
Online renewal is blocked if you renewed by mail or online during the previous renewal period, so the two remote channels cannot be used back to back. [A04]
Why it matters: group renewal; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-R10 | anchor: A05
For a mail renewal, an SC-licensed eye exam is shown by its receipt number, while an out-of-state eye exam is shown by enclosing the certificate itself. [A05]
Why it matters: group renewal; confusable receipt number versus certificate.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R11 | anchor: A06
A license expired nine months or less renews at a branch without tests, while one expired longer needs vision, knowledge and skills tests again. [A06]
Why it matters: group renewal; confusable nine months or less versus more.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R12 | anchor: A06
Points are posted to the SC record even when the traffic conviction happened in another state. [A06]
Why it matters: group points; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R13 | anchor: A07
Teen permit, conditional and special restricted holders are suspended at six points, while drivers 17 or older are suspended at 12 points. [A07]
Why it matters: group points; confusable teen versus adult suspension.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R14 | anchor: A07
The points behind an excessive-points suspension may also count toward a regular point system suspension. [A07]
Why it matters: group points; difficulty high.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R15 | anchor: A07
SCDMV-certified driving schools may offer the defensive driving course, and the right schools are those certified for the four-point reduction. [A07]
Why it matters: group points; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R16 | anchor: A08
Reinstatement questions go to the SCDMV online contact form, its phone line or any branch office, because suspension types vary widely. [A08]
Why it matters: group reinstatement; difficulty low.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-R17 | anchor: A09
A provisional license is limited to a first-offense DUI or DUAC suspension, and any later suspensions allowed alongside it must stem from that same violation. [A09]
Why it matters: group restricted licenses; confusable provisional versus other restricted licenses.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec02-R18 | anchor: A09
To qualify for a provisional license you must have or have had a valid SC license or be exempt, and must have met all requirements for earlier suspensions, revocations and cancellations. [A09]
Why it matters: group restricted licenses; difficulty high.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec02-R19 | anchor: A10
Accident judgment, alcohol violation, a 0.15 BAC, controlled substance, failing to stop for a blue light, false insurance certification, implied consent and misrepresentation of identity suspensions allow one route-restricted license per lifetime. [A10]
Why it matters: group restricted licenses; difficulty high.
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec02-R20 | anchor: A10
A route-restricted license application uses SCDMV form DL-127 and is mailed to SCDMV Driver Records. [A10]
Why it matters: group restricted licenses; difficulty medium.
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec02-R21 | anchor: A11
If the suspension is overturned, the Temporary Alcohol License must still be returned before you can apply for your regular license. [A11]
Why it matters: group restricted licenses; confusable sustained versus rescinded suspension.
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0028]

corpus_stability.reason: The South Carolina Driver's Manual prints a single edition line (Revised 06/2024) on its front cover; its disclaimer says legislative and SCDMV policy changes may make some content out of date until the agency incorporates them, and a possibly newer unlinked upload exists on the issuer site (freshness debt in the run jams), so the corpus is treated as revised at most about once a year, bound to the registered snapshot.
